vendors.name: Anchore Enterprise
vendors.offering: SBOM generation (Syft-based), storage and policy for containers and CI
vendors.pricing: not public; quote via sales (AWS Marketplace listing is contract-based, no single list price)

vendors.name: Docker Scout
vendors.offering: Generates/indexes image SBOMs and build attestations; vulnerability and policy views
vendors.pricing: bundled in Docker subscriptions: Personal $0 (1 Scout repo), Pro $9-11/user/mo (2 repos), Team $15-16/user/mo and Business $24/user/mo (unlimited Scout repos)

vendors.name: Snyk (SBOM export)
vendors.offering: CycloneDX/SPDX SBOM export for monitored open-source and container projects
vendors.pricing: Enterprise plan only; contact sales

vendors.name: FOSSA
vendors.offering: SCA and license compliance with SBOM generation and export
vendors.pricing: free tier plus Business tier; amount not verified

vendors.name: ReversingLabs Spectra Assure
vendors.offering: Binary analysis producing SBOMs and risk reports for built packages
vendors.pricing: quote; volume-based tiers, 14-day trial

vendors.name: SOOS
vendors.offering: SCA with SBOM generation and management
vendors.pricing: Community $0; Core SCA $99/month per TrustRadius

paid_market_gaps.gap: Generators disagree and omit dependencies; no vendor sells verified-accurate SBOMs across ecosystems
30-70% of manually installed packages in Docker images missed by common SBOM tools
SBOM export locked to Snyk Enterprise; SMBs needing compliance SBOMs pay enterprise prices
Binary/commercial-component SBOM coverage gated to higher ReversingLabs tiers; C/C++ builds poorly served

wtp_evidence: Generation itself is free (Syft, GitHub, Docker, Inspector); buyers pay only inside SCA/management bundles such as Snyk Enterprise or Anchore, not for generation alone.
bundling_note: GitHub exports SBOMs for anyone and AWS Inspector exports CycloneDX/SPDX at no extra cost, so basic generation is already free.
summary: Not a standalone business: generation is commoditized by OSS and bundled free by GitHub, Docker and AWS. Only an accuracy/verification layer for hard ecosystems (C/C++, binaries, hand-installed packages) might sell to regulated device makers.

vendors.name: Snyk Open Source
vendors.offering: Developer-first SCA with fix PRs for direct and transitive dependencies
vendors.pricing: Free tier; Team $25/contributing dev/month, 5-dev minimum, up to 10 contributing devs; Enterprise custom

vendors.name: GitHub Code Security (Dependabot)
vendors.offering: Dependabot alerts/updates plus premium dependency review bundled into GitHub
vendors.pricing: Code Security $30/active committer/month; basic Dependabot included with GitHub

vendors.name: Mend Renovate Enterprise / Mend SCA
vendors.offering: Automated dependency update PRs incl. transitive deps, merge confidence, SaaS or self-hosted
vendors.pricing: Renovate Enterprise $25,000/yr for 100 contributing devs (about $250/dev/yr) on AWS Marketplace; Mend SCA not public

vendors.name: Endor Labs
vendors.offering: SCA with function-level reachability and upgrade impact analysis to cut noise
vendors.pricing: not public (per contributing developer, quote)

vendors.name: Socket
vendors.offering: Dependency supply-chain security: malicious package detection and vulnerable dependency alerts
vendors.pricing: Free tier; Team about $25/dev/month, 5-dev minimum (third-party reports)

vendors.name: Semgrep Supply Chain
vendors.offering: SCA with reachability analysis bundled with Semgrep code scanning
vendors.pricing: Free up to 10 contributors; $30-40/contributor/month (sources conflict)

vendors.name: Aikido Security
vendors.offering: All-in-one AppSec platform incl. SCA with reachability and AutoFix
vendors.pricing: Free for 2 users; paid from about $300-350/month for 10 users (sources conflict)

vendors.name: Seal Security
vendors.offering: Backported patched library versions for unfixable or transitive vulnerable dependencies
vendors.pricing: not public

paid_market_gaps.gap: Transitive vulns blocked by parent version ranges or missing lockfile entries get no automatic fix PR
Per-developer pricing causes sticker shock as teams grow to 30-50 developers
Reachability and AutoFix locked to paid/enterprise tiers; free tiers only alert
No policy to fast-track security fixes past release-age cooldowns used against supply-chain attacks

wtp_evidence: Published SCA list prices cluster around $21-30/developer/month: Snyk Team $25/contributing dev/month, GitHub Code Security $30/active committer/month, Mend Renovate Enterprise $25,000/yr for 100 devs (about $21/dev/month). Buyers pay, but switch on price and free Dependabot sets a low baseline.
bundling_note: GitHub includes Dependabot alerts and security updates with the platform and sells Code Security add-ons, so baseline detect-and-bump is effectively free.
summary: Crowded, bundled market; no opening for another scanner. Narrow wedge: fixing the stuck cases (transitive conflicts, no-fix CVEs, cooldown-bypass policy) sold to teams already paying Snyk/GitHub, but Seal and Endor already target this.

vendors.name: WorkOS
vendors.offering: Enterprise SSO and Directory Sync (SCIM) APIs for B2B SaaS developers
vendors.pricing: Per connection: $125/mo for connections 1-15, falling to $65 at 51-100; SSO and SCIM billed as separate connections

vendors.name: Stytch
vendors.offering: B2B auth platform with SSO and SCIM connections from one shared pool
vendors.pricing: Pay-as-you-go: 5 SSO/SCIM connections free (shared pool), then $125 per connection/month; annual contract also sold via AWS Marketplace (see wtp_sources)

vendors.name: SSOJet
vendors.offering: Low-cost enterprise SSO and SCIM layer for SaaS apps
vendors.pricing: Business: $79 per connection/month billed monthly or $59 billed annually (2-4 connections; SSO and SCIM each count as one); volume discounts above; older listings show a $99/mo base structure

vendors.name: Ory Polis (formerly BoxyHQ SAML Jackson)
vendors.offering: Open-source enterprise SSO and SCIM 2.0 directory sync, self-host or managed
vendors.pricing: Open source self-hosted; managed/enterprise usage-based, price not public

vendors.name: Auth0 (Okta)
vendors.offering: CIAM platform with B2B enterprise connections and inbound SCIM
vendors.pricing: Free B2B tier includes 1 SSO connection plus SCIM (Feb 2026); B2B Essentials from $150/mo at 500 MAU; extra connections $100/mo

vendors.name: Clerk
vendors.offering: Developer auth platform bundling SCIM with enterprise connections
vendors.pricing: Pro $25/mo with one enterprise connection; SCIM bundled at no extra charge (vendor-authored source)

vendors.name: Stitchflow
vendors.offering: Provisions apps lacking SCIM via browser automation tied to Okta/Entra
vendors.pricing: Vendor claims under $5K per app per year; list price not public

vendors.name: Okta Lifecycle Management
vendors.offering: IdP-side automated provisioning/deprovisioning to SCIM-enabled apps
vendors.pricing: $4 per user per month add-on (bundled in Essentials suite from $17/user/month)

paid_market_gaps.gap: App buyers: 42-43% of 721 SaaS apps lock SCIM behind enterprise tiers; 57% offer no SCIM at all
Per-connection pricing bills SSO and SCIM separately, ~$250/mo per enterprise customer, painful for low-ACV SaaS
Okta customers must buy a $4/user/month Lifecycle Management add-on before SCIM provisioning works
Self-hosted/open-source auth stacks (SuperTokens, FusionAuth, better-auth) still lack native SCIM support

wtp_evidence: SaaS developers pay published per-connection prices: Stytch $125/mo after 5 free, or a $25,000/yr contract on AWS Marketplace; WorkOS and SSOJet per-connection prices are in the vendor rows. IT buyers pay enterprise-tier upgrades or Okta suites that include Lifecycle Management (Essentials from $17/user/month), but resent the SSO/SCIM tax.
bundling_note: Auth platforms now give SCIM away (Auth0 free B2B tier with SCIM, Clerk bundles it on Pro), compressing standalone SCIM-as-a-service pricing toward zero.
summary: Developer-side SCIM is crowded and being bundled free by Auth0/Clerk; little room. A narrower opening: buyer-side provisioning for apps without SCIM or with enterprise-locked SCIM (Stitchflow's niche), sold to mid-market IT teams.

vendors.name: Amazon RDS Proxy
vendors.offering: Managed DB proxy, now with end-to-end IAM authentication for RDS/Aurora MySQL and PostgreSQL
vendors.pricing: usage-based, per vCPU-hour (or per ACU-hour for Aurora Serverless), region-dependent

vendors.name: Teleport (Database Access / Machine & Workload Identity)
vendors.offering: Identity-aware proxy that uses IAM auth to RDS, issuing short-lived credentials
vendors.pricing: not public (quote-based; usage-based on monthly active users and Teleport Protected Resources, with each tbot machine-identity instance counted as a TPR, no separate per-MWI price)

vendors.name: StrongDM
vendors.offering: Infrastructure access proxy for databases, servers and Kubernetes with credential brokering
vendors.pricing: per user; third-party listings ~$50/user/month, AWS Marketplace Essentials $840/user/year

vendors.name: hoop.dev
vendors.offering: Identity-aware access gateway for databases including AWS RDS with IAM authentication
vendors.pricing: not public

vendors.name: Aembit Workload IAM
vendors.offering: Secretless workload-to-service access with credential injection and access policies
vendors.pricing: free Starter (10 workloads); Teams/Enterprise price not confirmed on vendor page

paid_market_gaps.gap: Popular third-party clients and ORMs (Prisma, kafka-go, ArgoCD) lack native AWS IAM auth; vendors don't sell client-side fixes.
RDS IAM auth caps around 200 new connections/second; the AWS workaround, RDS Proxy, adds per-vCPU cost.
Access proxies that broker IAM DB auth (Teleport, StrongDM) are quote-based or seat-minimum, heavy for small teams.
API Gateway IAM (SigV4) invocation from generic tooling relies on per-tool support that is often missing.

wtp_evidence: Buyers pay for broad access platforms: Vendr reports a StrongDM median of ~$33k/yr across 58 purchases, and its buyer guide shows a ~$71k average contract value that large deals skew upward. IAM itself is usable at no additional charge per AWS's RDS docs, so the per-client auth plumbing has no paid line item to displace.
bundling_note: AWS already ships IAM auth for RDS/MSK/Redshift/API Gateway plus free open-source signers in every major language and RDS Proxy, so remaining gaps get closed by AWS or OSS maintainers.
summary: Little standalone opening: the need is client-library plumbing that AWS and open source fill for free. Money only exists inside broader access-proxy platforms (Teleport, StrongDM), a crowded segment; at most a developer-tool feature, not a startup.

vendors.name: Cribl Stream
vendors.offering: Telemetry pipeline to filter, reduce, enrich and route logs before SIEM
vendors.pricing: Cribl.Cloud free up to 1 TB/day; paid Stream ingest credits ~$0.27/GB (Standard, up to 5 TB/day) to $0.32/GB (Enterprise), $1 per credit, plus worker infrastructure

vendors.name: DataBahn
vendors.offering: Security data pipeline; vendor-reported claims of up to 60% lower SIEM ingestion costs (Microsoft Sentinel integration) and 40-50% telemetry reduction
vendors.pricing: not public

vendors.name: Tenzir
vendors.offering: Security-focused pipeline engine (TQL) for SIEM, cloud and data cost optimization
vendors.pricing: Open-source edition free; commercial editions not public

vendors.name: Edge Delta Security Data Pipelines
vendors.offering: Edge-processed security pipelines with silent-source detection
vendors.pricing: not public (free trial)

vendors.name: Monad
vendors.offering: Security data ingestion and pipeline platform
vendors.pricing: not public on vendor site (AWS Marketplace listings exist, tier figures unverified)

vendors.name: Observo AI (SentinelOne)
vendors.offering: AI-native telemetry pipeline to enrich, summarize and route data; acquired by SentinelOne
vendors.pricing: not public

vendors.name: Onum (CrowdStrike)
vendors.offering: Real-time telemetry pipeline feeding Falcon Next-Gen SIEM; acquired by CrowdStrike
vendors.pricing: not public

vendors.name: Splunk Edge Processor
vendors.offering: Filter, mask, transform and route data before Splunk indexing
vendors.pricing: Included with Splunk Cloud Platform at no additional cost

paid_market_gaps.gap: Cribl's pricing and minimums are reviewed as unsuitable for small and medium companies
Pipeline tools need data-engineering effort to build and maintain; fit large SOCs, not small teams
Most security pipeline vendors publish no pricing; contact-sales only, blocking self-serve small-team buyers
Independent pipelines being absorbed by SIEM/XDR vendors, reducing vendor-neutral options

wtp_evidence: Enterprises pay per-GB pipeline fees (Cribl.Cloud ~$0.27-0.32/GB in credits above a free tier of up to 1 TB/day) to cut SIEM bills, and SIEM/XDR vendors buy pipeline startups (e.g. CrowdStrike agreed to acquire Onum); but Cribl's pricing and minimums are reviewed as unsuitable for small and medium companies, and the generous free tier caps what small teams would pay.
bundling_note: SIEM vendors bundle or buy pipelines: Splunk Edge Processor is free with Splunk Cloud, CrowdStrike bought Onum, SentinelOne bought Observo, Sentinel added cheap data-lake tiers.
summary: Crowded, well-funded enterprise market rapidly being bundled into SIEMs. Only a thin opening: self-serve, transparently priced, low-ops log reduction for small teams or MSSPs on Sentinel/Elastic/Wazuh, likely low ACV.

vendors.name: Aembit Workload IAM
vendors.offering: Workload IAM: secretless, policy-based access using native cloud identities across clouds
vendors.pricing: free Starter tier; Teams from $20/workload/month and $20/agent/month; Enterprise custom quote

vendors.name: Teleport Machine & Workload Identity
vendors.offering: Short-lived certificates and workload identity for machines, CI/CD and services
vendors.pricing: not public (bundled in Enterprise Standard; extra MWIs priced per unit)

vendors.name: Defakto (formerly SPIRL)
vendors.offering: SPIFFE-based non-human identity platform issuing short-lived workload identities
vendors.pricing: not public (subscription)

vendors.name: HCP Vault Dedicated (HashiCorp/IBM)
vendors.offering: Secrets manager with dynamic short-lived AWS credentials via AWS secrets engine
vendors.pricing: hourly cluster fee plus ~$112.17/client/month (Standard and Plus tiers, official HashiCorp price list)

vendors.name: Akeyless
vendors.offering: SaaS secrets and machine identity with workload identity federation across clouds
vendors.pricing: free 5 clients; paid tiers not public

vendors.name: Infisical
vendors.offering: Open-core secrets and machine identity with AWS IAM role-based auth
vendors.pricing: free tier; Pro $20/identity/month billed annually ($23 monthly); Advanced $40 annually

vendors.name: Oasis NHI Security Cloud (now Cyera Identity)
vendors.offering: Non-human identity discovery, posture and lifecycle management; Oasis acquired by Cyera (~$1B, 2026) and operates as Cyera Identity
vendors.pricing: AWS Marketplace Starter Pack $50,000/12 months

vendors.name: CyberArk (Palo Alto Networks)
vendors.offering: Machine identity, secrets management and PAM, now part of Palo Alto platform
vendors.pricing: not public

paid_market_gaps.gap: Per-identity/per-client pricing scales with machine count, punishing workload-heavy teams (Infisical Pro $20-23/identity, HCP Vault ~$112/client, Aembit $20/workload).
Paid secrets tools lag new AWS mechanisms: Vault lacked IAM Roles Anywhere; External Secrets broke on EKS Pod Identity.
Workload identity is mostly sold as quote-only enterprise bundles (Teleport, Defakto, Oasis $50k starter); Aembit Teams at $20/workload is the main self-serve exception.
Consolidation (CyberArk to Palo Alto, Astrix to Cisco) leaves buyers wary of standalone NHI vendor roadmaps.

wtp_evidence: Established paid products with public prices: HCP Vault Dedicated ~$112.17/client/month (Standard, official price list), Aembit Teams $20/workload/month, Oasis (now Cyera Identity) $50k/12-month starter on AWS Marketplace.
bundling_note: AWS gives IRSA, EKS Pod Identity and IAM Roles Anywhere (no service charge) plus SDK default-chain support for free, covering the core in-AWS and off-AWS need.
summary: AWS-only role credentials are free and native; paid money sits in multi-cloud workload identity/NHI platforms, already crowded and consolidating (Cyera-Oasis, Palo Alto-CyberArk). A narrow opening: cheap self-serve cross-cloud workload identity for mid-market teams, priced against per-identity Vault/Infisical bills and Aembit's $20/workload Teams tier.

vendors.name: Anchore Enterprise
vendors.offering: SBOM storage, CycloneDX/SPDX import-export, policy and compliance reporting
vendors.pricing: not public; quote via sales (AWS Marketplace contract listing prices deployment and support plan as separate dimensions, no single list price)

vendors.name: Interlynk

vendors.pricing: free Community tier; AWS Marketplace contracts by active developers: $18,000 (10), $36,000 (25), $60,000 (50), $100,000 (100)

vendors.pricing: Community free; Business from $159/month per third-party listing

vendors.name: Manifest

vendors.pricing: not public

vendors.name: Sonatype SBOM Manager

vendors.pricing: not public (contract-based on AWS Marketplace)

vendors.name: Cybeats SBOM Studio
vendors.offering: SBOM management, sharing and vulnerability monitoring
vendors.pricing: not public (quote)

vendors.name: ReversingLabs Spectra Assure
vendors.offering: SBOM import/export (incl. CycloneDX variants) with binary risk analysis
vendors.pricing: quote; tiers by SBOM import volume

vendors.name: Docker Scout
vendors.offering: Uses build-time SBOM attestations on images for policy and vulnerability analysis
vendors.pricing: free tier; Team $9 per repo/month

paid_market_gaps.gap: Artifact attestations for private repos require GitHub Enterprise Cloud; smaller teams can't tie SBOMs to releases cheaply
Management platforms mostly quote-only; few transparent-priced options for small manufacturers facing CRA SBOM duties
Inspector exports only CycloneDX 1.4; bundled exports lag current CycloneDX spec and VEX
SBOM-based vulnerability management yields noisy results; VEX workflow to suppress false positives remains immature

wtp_evidence: Public prices: Interlynk AWS Marketplace contracts $18k-$100k by active developers; sbomify Business from $159/month. Manifest won a three-year medical-device-maker deal (value undisclosed).
bundling_note: GitHub and Docker already bundle SBOM attestations at build, but cross-vendor SBOM/VEX lifecycle management and regulator-facing workflows are not given away by platforms.
summary: Modest opening: SBOM+VEX lifecycle management for SMB manufacturers facing EU CRA (Dec 2027) and FDA 524B, with transparent pricing. Crowded with funded specialists (Anchore, Manifest, Interlynk); attestation alone is bundled by GitHub/Docker.

vendors.name: Anchore Enterprise
vendors.offering: SBOM generation and management with vulnerability scanning, risk scoring and VEX annotations
vendors.pricing: not public

vendors.name: Manifest
vendors.offering: SBOM and VEX management separating theoretical CVEs from actual product exposure
vendors.pricing: not public
vendors.segment: enterprise; medical device makers (one disclosed multi-year deal)

vendors.name: Interlynk

vendors.pricing: not public; priced by active developer count, free trial

vendors.name: Cybeats SBOM Studio

vendors.pricing: not public; subscription by monitored SBOMs/products, not seats

vendors.name: Finite State

vendors.pricing: not public

vendors.name: JFrog Xray (Transitive SBOM)

vendors.pricing: not public in sources found

vendors.name: ArmorCode
vendors.offering: Continuous SBOM and VEX management for CRA product manufacturers
vendors.pricing: not public

vendors.name: ONEKEY
vendors.offering: Firmware SBOM and vulnerability analysis with compliance mapping, Dependency-Track alternative
vendors.pricing: not public

paid_market_gaps.gap: Teams on free Dependency-Track lack parent-component, container and vendor-advisory context; commercial tools are enterprise quote-only
Dependency-Track has no vendor-managed cloud with support and no reachability; no affordable hosted upgrade path
Ingesting vendor CSAF advisories to match against SBOMs is missing in common tooling
Transitive dependency graph views only work on some input types (bundled artifacts)

wtp_evidence: Funded SBOM/VEX vendors sell quote-based subscriptions (Manifest multi-year device-maker deal). CRA SBOM duty applies only from Dec 2027; Sept 2026 duties cover exploited-vulnerability/incident reporting. Prices not public.
bundling_note: AWS Inspector exports SBOMs free and JFrog/SCA suites add graph views, but cross-vendor VEX/CSAF product-impact analysis is not given away by clouds.
summary: Real but competitive opening: an affordable hosted SBOM impact/VEX layer (CSAF ingestion, dependency paths, container mapping) for mid-size software and device vendors preparing for CRA's Dec 2027 SBOM duty, between free Dependency-Track and enterprise quote-only platforms.
